subject.title: Crestodian chat hijacks natural language into operations; approvals require a literal hardcoded yes

question: Should Crestodian normal chat become strictly AI-first, with deterministic parsing limited to exact typed commands and rescue/no-model fallback?
rationale: The source shows real bugs, but the requested endpoint changes setup UX, fallback semantics, approval intent, and security boundaries across CLI, Gateway, and rescue surfaces.

options.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
options.body: Route normal natural language to the agent or planner, keep only exact typed commands deterministic, and repair approval, stale proposals, redaction, and Gemini parity together.

options.title: Ship parser safety first
options.body: Anchor the riskiest command regexes and broaden literal approval handling while deferring AI-first and executor refactor work.

options.title: Split the umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue canonical but require smaller follow-ups for parser safety, approval intent, stale proposals, secret redaction, executor refactor, and Gemini parity.

recommendation.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
recommendation.body: Route normal natural language to the agent or planner, keep only exact typed commands deterministic, and repair approval, stale proposals, redaction, and Gemini parity together.

likelyOwner.reason: The current and historical Crestodian feature path points to steipete as the best available product and safety-boundary owner.
